title: UCC § 2-207 — formation and unmatched terms
summary: Analyze a definite acceptance or confirmation, express conditionality, term incorporation, and any contract created by conduct as separate steps.
notes: Subsection (1) recognizes a definite and seasonable expression of acceptance or timely confirmation despite additional or different terms, subject to its expressly conditional proviso. Subsection (2) treats additions as proposals and supplies the between-merchants rule and its exceptions. Subsection (3) addresses conduct recognizing a contract despite insufficient writings and provides agreed terms plus supplementary Code terms. The chapter gives extensive quotations and applications, but the complete SEL text and comments should still be kept as a separate assigned source. Northrop’s dispute about different terms and Hill’s one-form argument must be recorded as disagreements, rather than smoothed into one rule.

priorVersions.summary: Separate formation by an expression of acceptance or confirmation, treatment of additional terms, and formation by conduct.
priorVersions.notes: Subsection (1) includes the expressly conditional proviso. Subsection (2) specifies treatment of additional terms and exceptions between merchants. Subsection (3) addresses conduct when writings do not establish a contract. Courts differ on some issues, including different terms; add the assigned cases and applicable law.
